q1.question: What is local SEO and how does it differ from regular SEO?
q1.answer: Local SEO is search engine optimisation specifically for location-based searches - like 'plumber in Sofia' or 'dentist near me'. Unlike traditional SEO that targets standard organic results, local SEO focuses on the 'map pack' - the three businesses displayed on Google Maps. These searches have the highest buyer intent of any search type.

q2.question: What is Google Business Profile and do I need one?
q2.answer: Google Business Profile (GBP) is the free business listing that controls how your company appears on Google Maps and Search. Without a verified and optimised GBP, it is virtually impossible to rank in the Top 3. It is the foundation of everything we do - without it, even the best optimisation cannot work.

q3.question: Do I need a website to rank on Google Maps?
q3.answer: Not strictly required, but strongly recommended. A website sends additional authority signals to Google. When you have a website we can edit, we include website optimisation too. If you don't have a website, we can still help - but results will be significantly stronger with one.

q1.question: What exactly does your service include?
q1.answer: The work includes: full competitor analysis, Google Business Profile optimisation (categories, attributes, photos, description, Q&A), high-quality citation and authority signal building, and bi-weekly updates. When you have a website we can edit, we also include full website optimisation. A check of your visibility in AI assistants is included, with no promise of results.

q2.question: Can you help us get more Google reviews?
q2.answer: Yes. We provide proven strategies and templates for collecting reviews without violating Google's policies. Reviews are a key ranking signal - more quality reviews directly improve your position in the map pack and build trust with potential customers.

q3.question: Which industries do you work with?
q3.answer: We work with any local business that serves customers face-to-face: plumbers, dentists, lawyers, accountants, auto repair shops, restaurants, hotels, beauty salons, gyms, and many more. If your customers search for businesses like yours on Google - we can help.

q4.question: What happens after the initial 90-day period?
q4.answer: After the 90-day initial phase you continue month to month, with 30 days' notice. We work to maintain and strengthen your position because the competitive landscape shifts over time.

q1.question: How quickly will we see movement in rankings?
q1.answer: First movement is usually visible within 4–6 weeks in low competition and 8–12 weeks in higher competition. These are guidelines, not promises. We discuss a conditional guarantee only after an audit.

q2.question: How do you track and report progress?
q2.answer: We monitor your Google Maps ranking weekly using specialist tools. You receive bi-weekly updates with concrete data on your ranking position, impressions, and user actions - calls, direction requests, and website visits.

q3.question: What if our competitors are also doing local SEO?
q3.answer: Competitor analysis is the first step of our process. We know exactly what the top-ranking businesses are doing and how to outpace their strategy. In 9 out of 10 cases, our clients reach the Top 3 even when competitors are actively investing in local SEO.

q4.question: What are citations and why do they matter?
q4.answer: A citation is any online mention of your business that includes your name, address, and phone number (NAP). Google uses the consistency and quality of these mentions as a trust signal. We build high-quality citations in authoritative, industry-specific directories relevant to your location.

Internet marketing is a broad term: advertising, social media, email, content, SEO. This page explains where local organic SEO fits, when it is the right first move for a local business and when it is not enough on its own.

sections.title: What internet marketing includes for a local business
paragraphs: For a company serving customers in a specific city or district there are usually five channels. Paid advertising (Google Ads, Meta Ads) brings quick traffic but stops the moment the budget stops. Social media builds awareness and community. Email and Viber communication keep existing customers. Content and a blog answer questions before purchase. Local SEO makes sure people who are already searching for your service in Google see you - in Google Maps and in organic results.
No channel is best for everyone. The choice depends on whether your customers actively search (for example "dentist in Lozenets") or first need to be convinced they need the service.

sections.title: Where local SEO fits
paragraphs: When someone searches for a service with intent to buy, often the same day, the local results in Google Maps are among the first things they see. That is where Atlas Fold works: we optimise the Google Business Profile, the website and local citations so the business is clearly described and appears for relevant searches.

The advantage is that the effort accumulates: a well-built profile and website keep working after the active work ends. The limitation is that results are not instant and depend on competition in your niche and district. That is why we do not promise a specific position - we show what is realistic after auditing your case.

sections.title: What we do and what we do not do
items: Google Business Profile optimisation - categories, services, description, photos, posts.
On-page SEO - titles, structure, internal links, local pages, structured data.

Review strategy - how to collect genuine reviews within Google's rules.
We do not manage Google Ads, Meta Ads or social profiles. If you need them we will say so and recommend handing them to a specialist.
sections.outro: This narrow scope is deliberate: an agency that does everything rarely does everything equally well.

sections.title: When local SEO is the right first move
paragraphs: It most often fits businesses where the customer comes to you, or you go to the customer, within a defined area: dentists, beauty salons, car workshops, gyms, lawyers, building and repair firms, restaurants. It also fits when you already have a Google profile but it is incomplete or not showing.

It is not the best start if you sell nationwide online, if you do not yet have a working business with fixed services, or if you need customers this week. In that case paid advertising gives a faster signal, and local SEO runs in parallel as a long-term investment.

whatIs.title: What is local SEO and why does it matter for Sofia businesses

howGoogle.title: How Google ranks local businesses in Sofia - the three signals
howGoogle.intro: The Google Maps algorithm evaluates who to show in the local 3-pack based on three criteria. Understanding them is the foundation of any sound Sofia SEO strategy.

relevance.title: Relevance - does Google understand what you do?
relevance.p1: Relevance measures how well your Google Business Profile matches the searcher's intent. Key components: primary category (it must be your single most-searched service, not a broad description), additional categories (up to 9 additional ones, layered precisely), business description with the primary search term in the first 250 characters, a services list using the exact terms your customers search for, and Posts maintaining profile freshness.
relevance.p2: The problem we see in Sofia audits: businesses pick a general category and don't add the specialized sub-categories. A dental clinic listed only as 'Doctor' competes against thousands of results. Listed as 'Dental Clinic' + 'Dental Implants' + 'Pediatric Dentistry' + 'Cosmetic Dentistry' - it competes against dozens.

authority.title: Authority - does Google trust it?
authority.p1: Authority is built from three types of signals. Reviews: count, average rating, velocity of new reviews, and owner response quality. A profile with 200 reviews and responses to 80% of them is significantly more trusted than a profile with 200 reviews and no responses at all. Citations: mentions of the business with a consistent NAP (Name, Address, Phone) on bgmaps.com, navimaps.bg, pozvanete.bg, 0700.bg, and industry-specific directories. Links: contextually relevant references from Bulgarian sites - partnerships, press mentions, local news.
authority.p2: NAP consistency is underestimated. If your business appears as 'Dr. Ivanov Ltd' on one site and 'Dr. Ivanov' on another - Google registers two different entities and reduces trust in both. A single address discrepancy - 'Dunav St. 5' vs '5 Dunav Street' - is enough.

distance.title: Distance - how proximity factors in (and how much)
distance.p1: Distance is the only one of the three factors you cannot change. Google measures the distance between the business and the searcher - or, for searches without a specific location, between the business and the neighborhood centroid (the center of the searched area). A business in the center of Lozenets will have a distance advantage over a business on the edge of the neighborhood for imprecise searches.

We've seen a business 1.5km from the Lozenets centroid outrank a business 200m away, simply because the profile and citations were incomparably better. Distance sets the ceiling; relevance and authority determine whether you reach it.
